title: Sudden awakening
hook: Huineng's southern school taught that awakening is sudden; the northern school stressed the gradual

segments.voice: Yesterday, no-thought: thoughts come and go, and the mind isn't carried off. Your line: not stuck. Did one circling thought arrive and leave without you on board? Day one thousand two hundred eighteen.

Anyone who learned to ride a bike can tell it two ways. One way: it took weeks. Scraped knees, a hand on the back of the seat, more wobbly starts than anyone counted. The other way: it happened in an instant. One afternoon the hand let go, and suddenly you were riding. Both stories are true. They're just told from different ends. Chan Buddhism in China told its own version of this argument, about awakening, and attached it to two teachers we've already met at the wall with their verses. Today: sudden awakening.
screen: `IT TOOK WEEKS.` → `IT HAPPENED IN AN INSTANT.` → `BOTH STORIES ARE TRUE.`

segments.voice: First, the two names. The Platform Sutra speaks of a southern teaching and a northern one: Huineng in the south, Shenxiu in the north, and it links the south with sudden awakening and the north with the gradual. Second, the verses show the two emphases. Shenxiu's verse said: wipe the mirror again and again, let no dust settle. That's patient, steady practice, a little cleaner each day. Huineng's answered: from the beginning there is nothing for dust to land on. That's seeing, all at once, what was already so. Third, and this is the surprise: the sutra doesn't let the argument end there. In paraphrase, Huineng says the teaching itself is neither sudden nor gradual. People are quicker or slower, and that is where the difference lies. The way is one. The pace belongs to the walker. Read like that, sudden and gradual are not rival camps. They are the bike story told from both ends: the long wobbling, and the instant it clicks. Fourth, a look back at this week, which has had both in it. The Xinxin Ming said the great way is not hard, without picking and choosing. Then a hair's breadth, and heaven and earth apart. Don't seek the true, just stop holding opinions. Not two. Then a woodcutter who heard a sutra through a doorway, and no-thought, not stuck. Any one of those can land in an instant. Any one of them can also take years of mornings to live.
screen: `SOUTH SUDDEN, NORTH GRADUAL.` · `TWO VERSES, TWO EMPHASES.` · `THE TEACHING HAS NO SPEEDS.` · `A WEEK OF BOTH.` · then, large: `SUDDEN AND GRADUAL.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice, if you'd like. Sit and let the breath come. Notice that each breath arrives whole, all at once, the moment it's here. And notice, too, that the sitting settles slowly, a little at a time. Let both be true. Then bring to mind someone whose way is different from yours: someone who goes slowly where you rush, or leaps where you plod. Hold them in mind for a few breaths with some respect, as another walker on the same road. The bell holds the time.

Sudden awakening. The teaching the Platform Sutra links with Huineng's southern school, beside the north's gradual way, and the sutra's own reminder that the teaching itself has no speeds. Today's word.
Your line: sudden and gradual. Today, when someone learns at a different pace than you, let both ways have their place. Day one thousand two hundred eighteen.

screen: `DAY 1218 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: THE ROBE NOT PASSED ON.`

howItsDone: Zen and Chan schools discuss sudden and gradual awakening in talks and study, and some teachers present them as two sides of practice rather than rival paths.

fork.setup: in Huineng's own sutra, the question comes up: is the way sudden or gradual? what does the text answer?
options: sudden, and the gradual is wrong
the teaching is neither; people are quicker or slower
gradual, but nobody should say so
fork.reveal: even in the sutra of the 'sudden' school, Huineng says the teaching has no sudden or gradual. the difference is in people.

original.note: Chinese (dunwu): 'sudden awakening', the teaching the Platform Sutra links with the south.

trapdoor: what you thought: sudden awakening means enlightenment with no practice.
what it means: seeing at once what was already so, beside a gradual way of steady practice.
what a scholar hears: the Platform Sutra links south with sudden and north with gradual, yet has Huineng say the teaching itself is neither; the difference is in people.

notes: Check the line 'the teaching has no sudden or gradual; people are sharp or dull' (法無頓漸，人有利鈍) and the south/north framing (南能北秀) in the version the Keeper prefers.
Kept the two schools unranked on purpose. Keeper may wish to add that the sudden/gradual polemic was sharpened by later southern-school writers; left out of the voice under the claims rule.
Editor pass: 'many teachers' softened to 'some'; cleared a vague sentence in the look-back ('doing exactly this'); changed 'every one of them takes a lifetime' to a hedged 'can also take years'.
